question: How do some thinkers describe cognition across all distinctions?
premises: Some assign cognitive status to every distinction of every measured thing.
They say this cognition arises in sequence everywhere.
They also allow that in some cases it arises without sequence.
inference: This view treats cognition as operating through all distinctions, sometimes sequentially and sometimes non-sequentially.
uncertainties: The compressed compound in token 3 is doctrinally dense; the gloss follows the most direct reading.
plain_english: Others hold that every distinction of every measured thing has the status of cognition, arising in sequence everywhere and in some cases arising without sequence.
